title: Add a command that runs independent queued jobs in parallel
summary: Today `athena go` runs one job per invocation, and queued jobs (`ask --later`) must be read and run by hand one after another. I read the request as: let one command (`athena go` with several jobs, or `--all`) run independent jobs concurrently, with a bounded worker count, reusing the existing per-job and repository locks.

defaults_applied.how: Recovered the intended shape from the CLI, run.rs locks, and design §5.5 and the deferred-work table instead of asking.
One focused change: a multi-job go with a bounded worker count, no scheduler.
New tests with fake agents for concurrency, landing, and stale cases; clippy and fmt clean.
Pure Rust with std threads; no new non-Rust files.
Prefer std::thread::scope; add a crate only if clearly needed, and record the call.
The design doc and decision log are updated with alternatives.
Behavior is verified by cargo test with the fake agent, which exercises the parallel path.

assumptions: 'Independent' means jobs in different states of the same repository that share no dependencies; Athena has no dependency model in v0, so the user chooses which jobs go together.
Parallelism is within one process using threads, built on the existing safety: per-job locks (try_lock_job), the repository lock for fast-forward landing, and per-job snapshots (design §5.5).
A job that goes stale because another landed first is reported as stale, not automatically re-verified; the design lists an automatic re-verify scheduler as deferred.
A concurrency limit defaults to a small number; the spend limits and kill switch apply unchanged.
The shape is `athena go <job>... [--jobs N]` plus `--all` for every queued/proposed job; the single-job behavior and exit codes stay the same.
Athena and its dependencies can be shared across threads; if not, the minimal fix is in scope.

acceptance_criteria.text: `cargo test` passes, including a new test that runs at least two fake-agent jobs through the parallel path and shows both reach a terminal state, with overlapping run intervals or a barrier proving concurrency.
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
A test shows that two parallel jobs that touch different files both land with records intact, and two that conflict leave the later one stale or blocked, never merged silently.
`cargo run -p athena-cli -- go --help` documents the multi-job / parallel option and the concurrency limit.
Single-job `athena go <job>` keeps its output and exit codes (0 landed, 2 not landed, 1 error); the multi-job result reports one line per job and exits 2 if any did not land.
A job already locked by another process is reported for that job without aborting the others.
The kill switch and per-job budgets are applied to every parallel job; the code path honors refuse_if_stopped.
Design doc (command table, §5.5, deferred-work table), README, and CHANGELOG describe the new behavior; a decision entry records the choice and alternatives (threads vs. separate processes).

out_of_scope: An automatic scheduler or merge queue that re-verifies stale jobs.
Job decomposition, dependencies, or chunking a request into several jobs.
Changes to governance files such as athena.toml, defaults.toml, or CI workflows.
departures: Higher cost and longer wall time than the reference: concurrency in the core run path plus tests and design docs is larger than a typical job, and the request is ambiguous about the shape, which lowers acceptance.
